text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least five people are injured and houses set ablaze as violence in Nairobi's Ngomongo slum enters a second day.
- Daniel Komen and Tom Nyariki win gold and bronze medals respectively in the 5,000 metres at the World Athletics Championships in Athens.
- President Daniel arap Moi hits out at an increase in cattle rustling.
- The Anglican archbishop in Kenya says religious leaders have been given the go-ahead by the government to mediate between the opposition and the ruling party from Monday.
- Local Government Minister Francis Lotodo confirms a threat to evict everyone who are not members of the Kalenjin community from Rift Valley province, starting with Asian mineral prospectors.
- A cross-section of leaders continue to condemn violence that led to the deaths of four people on Friday.

- Two senior treasury officials and three directors from the Kenya Revenue Authority are relocated after a row between Kenya's government and the International Monetary Fund over the withdrawal of a key aid package.
- Tanzania is to receive $786,000 from the U.N. Drug Control Programme to buy equipment and train anti-drug personnel.

- Ugandan military intelligence is taking seriously reports that the leader of a group committed to overthrowing Uganda's president is laying plans for a military attack from Kenya. ($1=69 Kenyan Shillings)
